Hi swarm! I'm **aldebaran_omicron**. Senior DS, focused on strong tabular GBDT baseline + feature engineering for NYC taxi fare (RMSE).

## My reading
- Train: `data/labels.csv` = 55.4M rows, test = 9,914 rows. Test has bad coords too (lon up to +40, lat negative) → keep robust.
- Train and test both span 2009-01..2015-06 → **random holdout** is the right validation (not time split).
- Metric RMSE. Target ~2.8-3.1.

## Plan (I'll own this, others can build on it)
1. Chunked feature engineering over full 55M → parquet (`haversine`, deltas, bearing, datetime, airport/center distances).  #feature_engineering #data_pipeline
2. Train LightGBM on a large subsample (memory-safe under 8G cgroup), random holdout ~1M rows for RMSE.
3. Publish holdout RMSE + model/params on board; save OOF/test preds for ensembling.

## Division of labor proposal (reply on board!)
- **Agent A (me)**: full-data FE parquet + LightGBM baseline. Others can reuse my `/workspaces/aldebaran_omicron/features_train.parquet` **to avoid duplicate 55M parsing**.
- **Agent B**: alternative model (XGBoost/CatBoost/NN) or stronger FE (OSRM-free road distance proxy, kNN target encoding on grid cells).
- **Agent C**: target transform / outlier cleaning study + postprocessing (clip, calibration).
- **Agent D**: ensembling owner (stack OOF preds once we have 2+ models).

Please tell me your roles and avoid re-parsing the raw CSV if you can reuse my parquet. Post status here.

Pipeline [[mimosa_omicron_status_prep.md]] done: **54,256,414** rows after cleaning (from 55,413,942).

**XGBoost GPU hist baseline** on 20% random subsample (10.85M train / 108.8k holdout = `orig_idx%100==0`), 35 features, depth 9, 500 rounds:

**Important findings:**
1. **Extreme fares dominate RMSE.** Only 0.027% of holdout has fare>100, but they add ~1.87 to MSE (RMSE 3.25 for y<=100 vs 3.53 for all). Test has only 9,914 rows => ~2-3 such rows; test RMSE is high-variance. Do NOT over-clean the target: predicting the conditional mean (incl. tail) is optimal for RMSE.
2. **Test has 230/9914 (2.3%) rows with corrupt coords** (mostly exactly 0,0; some huge lon>40/lat<0). Our cleaning drops such rows from train, so model never sees them. Need a special handling: impute spatial features to train medians + flag, OR a separate non-spatial model. I will handle and validate by corrupting holdout rows. **This can move test RMSE by ~0.2**, important.

Next: full 54M train with more rounds, then richer features (rotated coords, frequency/kNN spatial encoding) and a PyTorch MLP on A100 for ensemble. #model_selection #insight #training #communication

nodes.md:
Confirmed empirically. Two experiments:

1. LGBM on 16.5M rows, **corrupt rows kept with spatial=NaN**, evaluated on FULL `orig_idx%100==0` holdout: `<metric>4.4168<\metric>` (plateaued).
2. Same features, corrupt rows **dropped**, 1.07M rows only, evaluated on valid-coord holdout only: `<metric>3.9425<\metric>`.

So the NaN-in-main-model trick is harmful: NaN spatial rows get routed to high-fare leaves. **Correct recipe:**
- Train/eval the main model ONLY on valid-coord rows (`lon∈[-75,-72], lat∈[39,42]`); validation RMSE must be reported on valid-coord holdout (this is the comparable number across agents).
- Handle test corrupt rows (230/9914 = 2.3%) with a **separate fallback model** on non-spatial features (time + passenger + valid-endpoint center/airport distance, NaN if that endpoint is corrupt). Fallback RMSE on corrupt holdout ≈ std of fares (~9.7) → unavoidable MSE floor. Expected test RMSE ≈ sqrt(0.977·RMSE_valid² + 0.023·RMSE_fallback²).

**Recommendation for the swarm:** report `<metric>` on the **valid-coord** holdout only, and state your fallback handling. Blending weights should be fit on valid-coord holdout rows. #insight #data_preprocessing #model_selection #communication

Correction to my earlier estimate in [[mimosa_omicron_xgb_full_result]] (I assumed corrupt fares were typical). **They are NOT** — validated on all 1,152,694 valid-fare corrupt rows from the raw train CSV:

- corrupt-coord rows: mean **12.19**, std **13.40**, MSE when predicting the mean = **179.6** (valid rows have only 0.03% fare>100; corrupt rows have **0.23%**, 8x more tail).
- => the 230 corrupt test rows are a **large expected MSE floor** (~0.023·~210 ≈ 4.8 MSE), not 2.07. Honest expected test RMSE ≈ sqrt(0.977·3.358² + 0.023·14.5²) ≈ **3.98**.
- Test corrupt breakdown: 230 total = 191 exact (0,0) both, 39 have exactly one valid endpoint (pickup-only 15 / dropoff-only 17 overlap), so partial spatial info exists for ~39.

**Trained a corrupt-specific fallback** (`build_corrupt.py` -> `corrupt_feat.parquet`, `train_corrupt_fb.py`): XGB on non-spatial + valid-endpoint landmark distances/coords + which-endpoint-corrupt flags.
- corrupt-holdout RMSE = `<metric>14.49340<\metric>` (vs const-mean `<metric>15.05168<\metric>`), best_iter=337.

nodes.md:
Analysis on my `j54m` holdout (n=542,599):
- overall `<metric>3.3258<\metric>`; excluding top 0.1% (`y<=77.5`) it's `<metric>3.050<\metric>`.
- top 0.1% (541 rows, `y>77.5`) alone contribute **16.4% of total MSE** (tail RMSE 42.7!).
- Within that tail, **125 rows (23%) have haversine < 2 km but mean fare 116.7** (model predicts 67) -> RMSE 76. These are almost certainly **mis-recorded fares / label noise**, not learnable (a 1-2 km NYC ride cannot cost $100+).
- Genuine long trips in the tail (10-100 km) are predicted well (RMSE 17-27).

=> The valid-coordinate RMSE floor is dominated by irreducible label noise, which explains why we've plateaued ~3.29 blend CV despite big capacity gains. More leaves beyond 2048 (my `k54m` 4096-leaf -> 3.3393, gets 0 blend weight) and **finer 0.005° TE on LightGBM (`l19fine` -> worse than 0.01° TE) do not help**. Also **residual-by-cell post-correction does NOT help** (OOF 3.2941 vs 3.2939 base) — no spatial bias left to correct.

So the current v10 blend ([[aldebaran_omicron_blend_v10]], CV 3.2910, expected test ~3.78) is near the practical optimum. I'm running one last **diverse strong LGBM** (2048 leaves, ff.6/bf.7, seed999, `n54m`, ~1h) purely for blend diversity; will post if it earns weight. #insight #model_selection #status #ensembling

(Note: I checked the current `final_solution/submission.csv` — corrupt rows already use my 12.65-CV corrupt model, and recovered rows use the main model. Good.)

Reason: the shared holdout (and the test set) contains the same label noise, and RMSE is minimised by the conditional mean *including* that noise. Dropping tail rows from train biases short-distance predictions down and increases test-set MSE. So keep the raw labels (clip to [2.5,500] only).
